reasoning: The broad problem — dishonest debaters degrading weak-judge accuracy by obscuring rather than falsifying evidence — is well studied. The QuALITY single-decisive-quote debate testbed is standard (Michael et al. 2023; Khan et al. 2024), and the "obfuscated arguments problem" (Barnes/Christiano; Prover-Estimator Debate, arXiv:2506.13609) directly concerns dishonest debaters burying flaws so judges can do no better than chance, with verbosity-bias and word-limit mitigations also documented. However, the specific operationalization proposed here — augmenting the dishonest side with a *growing count* of true-but-irrelevant quotes drawn from the same passage to dilute the one decisive quote, measuring an accuracy-vs-distractor-count curve, and testing a targeted "rank the single most decisive piece of evidence first" judge prompt as mitigation — does not appear in the surveyed literature. Existing obfuscation work centers on intractable subproblem decomposition and probability-assignment protocols, not evidence dilution within quote-based single-passage debate, so the precise attack/mitigation pairing is unexplored.

evidence.title: Debating with More Persuasive LLMs Leads to More Truthful Answers (Khan et al., 2024)
evidence.summary: Establishes the QuALITY quote-based debate testbed with weak judges; finds natural-language arguments and quote use affect judge accuracy. Confirms the standard setting and that quote handling is central, but does not study graded distractor dilution or a decisive-quote ranking mitigation.

evidence.title: Debate Helps Supervise Unreliable Experts (Michael et al., 2023)
evidence.summary: Shows 52% of consultancy errors come from debaters obfuscating relevant evidence from the judge, and discusses how dishonest debaters cite unrelated context-shifting quotes. Closest to the dilution problem but treats obfuscation qualitatively, without a controlled distractor-count experiment or the proposed ranking prompt.

evidence.title: Avoiding Obfuscation with Prover-Estimator Debate
evidence.summary: Formalizes the obfuscated arguments problem (dishonest debater makes flaw localization intractable) and proposes a probability-assignment protocol mitigation. Addresses the general 'burying' failure mode but via structural protocol change, not evidence dilution within single-passage quote debate or a judge-prompt mitigation.

evidence.title: Debate update: Obfuscated arguments problem
evidence.summary: Original articulation that a dishonest debater can construct arguments where the flaw is true-looking but hard to locate, reducing the judge to random guessing. Conceptually adjacent to dilution but about intractable subproblem decomposition, not padding a decisive quote with true-but-irrelevant quotes.

evidence.title: Towards Scalable Oversight with Collaborative Multi-Agent Debate in Error Detection (2025)
evidence.summary: Documents 'debate hacking' where debaters mislead judges with overconfident/misframed claims and proposes a collaborative protocol mitigation. Shows active interest in judge-misleading attacks and mitigations, but neither the specific dilution attack nor the decisive-evidence-ranking prompt is tested.
